title: Ordinary tensor adjoint comparison and normalized completion square
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime ell different from its characteristic, a separated quasi-compact locally finite-type scheme X over its algebraic closure, and a finite coefficient field E over Q_ell. For every normalized ordinary tensor presentation a [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models], every normalized ordinary-to-completed comparison c [def-sf-rational-verdier-data], and integral constructible objects K,N [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let S be the integral closed structure of the coefficient calculus [def-pur-completed-pullback-tower-core], and let e_K be the unique counit-preserving comparison a.tensor(K,-) to S.tensor(-,K) from uniqueness of left adjoints to the same internal Hom. Then e_K(N) followed by the canonical completion unit on (N,K) [def-sf-integral-completion-transpose] equals c(K,N) followed by the canonical completed signed braiding [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-constraints]. This is an equation of actual ambient integral tensor maps, without a Hom-constructibility or rational-identification hypothesis.

source.place: Paragraph 1, normalized integral evaluation and its coefficient comparison; ordinary-to-completed tensor normalization.

proof.text: Use the ordinary tensor-Hom adjunction of a and the canonical coefficient calculus adjunction to form leftAdjointUniq. On K-flat inputs and K-injective targets the counit normalization of a and the canonical signed evaluation identify this comparison with the K-flat model interchange. The Koszul interchange accounts for precisely the sign in a.evaluation. Test against all K-injective targets to identify the comparison itself.

Compose the comparison with the actual reduction/limit tensor unit on the exchanged inputs. In the two Roos coordinates, compare this map to the supplied completion c followed by the canonical completed braiding: their quotient components are the same signed pure tensor and their shifted components vanish. Tensor-completion-chain uniqueness identifies the augmentations. The representative equation of c and the normalized coefficient calculus comparisons identify the derived maps.

Descend the equality from simultaneous flat-term K-flat representatives by the product localization. Equivalently use faithful coherent reduction after its normalized tensor comparisons. Resolve both constructible inputs to obtain the displayed component equation. No Hom-pair assumption, target object, duality datum, or rational localization occurs in this step.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryCompletedTensor_adjoint_square
    (a : IntegralHom.TensorPresentation.{u, u} X
      (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E X))
    (c : RationalVerdier.Completion D l hl X E a)
    (K N : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X) :
    ((a.adjunction K.obj).leftAdjointUniq
      ((pullbackTensorCalculus l E X).integralClosed.adjunction K.obj)).hom.app N.obj ≫
        podCompletedTensorUnit l E X N.obj K.obj =
      c.map.app (K.obj, N.obj) ≫
        (@pullbackTensorIntegralBraiding l _ E _ _ _ X
          (RationalVerdier.units D l hl X) K N).hom.hom
